added_lines: safeguarding sunday 22nd february 2026 training a special word of thanks to our diocesan safeguarding trainers, trish o’neill & ailish higgins who facilitated 10 training events in 2025. a total number of 177 church personnel, including clergy, religious, staff and volunteers trained in 2025. the diocesan safeguarding committee joined the ossory safeguarding committee and attended training facilitated by the national board in kilkenny 17th november 2025. the training focused on the role of safeguarding committees in the context of our national church policy and standards for safeguarding children. clonaslee

following the 2024 launch of the church’s child safeguarding policy, ailish higgins, our diocesan director of safeguarding met with young people from the diocese to ask them “what does a safe & welcoming church mean to you?” thanks to all the children and young people who took part in these sessions and were open and honest about their experience of parish life. thanks too to their parents, the group leaders and parish priests who supported the facilitation of these groups. national board for safeguarding children in the catholic church in ireland – biannual conference the held their biannual conference from 3rd – 5th september 2025 titled: towards a restorative and transitional justice model of engaging with victims and survivors in the catholic church in ireland. the event aimed to enhance the understanding we all have of how we must engage in a just and restorative way with those who have suffered harm in the catholic church in ireland. our diocesan director of safeguarding and dlp attended the event and shared valuable feedback with our diocesan safeguarding committee. the learning from the conference will help guide our practice going forward. special thanks to the national board for organising and hosting the event. youth participation amadeus christmas clane confirmation class safeguarding checklist for parishes displayed in all church porches the kildare & leighlin child safeguarding statement poster dated 2024 and signed by bishop nulty (please remove all old statement posters, these are now obsolete). child friendly safeguarding poster parish webcam and cctv notice/poster towards healing poster in the sacristy register – spine bound book to be signed by all who enter the sacristy (to be used even when no altar servers present, available for purchase from faith development services. celebret request poster codes of behaviour (one for adults, and one for servers where applicable). local safeguarding representatives have completed recruitment process and full diocesan safeguarding training have clear role description (leaflets available on role of lsr) have completed vetting process. be aware of dlp contact details. be aware of reporting procedures for allegations of abuse. support parish priest with ensuring all activities with children/ young people and vulnerable adults are in line with church policy. support parish priest with completion of the annual safeguarding self-adult. staff & volunteers working with children / young people have completed recruitment process and appropriate diocesan safeguarding training. have completed vetting process. ensure consent forms are completed. maintain a record of attendance for all activities involving under 18s. codes of behaviour in place for adult leaders and children/ young people. risk assessment for activities involving under 18s to be completed annually, sample document on diocesan website. john paul awards youth pilgrimage to rome

hay & oats collection (annual collection for priest of the parish) we have come to that time of year again for our hay and oats collection. first of all, i would like to thank you sincerely for your continued and generous support of our parish. as you may know we have two accounts in our parish: 1. parish account; 2. clergy account. thanks to your continued support our parish account is in relatively good standing. our clergy account has understandably bottomed out and we have had to borrow money from our parish account to keep the clergy account solvent. all the contributions that come in from the hay and oats will be lodged into the clergy account. representatives in your area will drop in an envelope into your house over the next week or two. it would be greatly appreciated if you could place your donation into the envelope and drop it back to your representative or, into the parish office, or into mass at the weekend. we would be grateful if you could put your correct address and eircode on the front of the envelope. once again, a sincere "thank you" for your continued support. we also appreciate the hard work of our parish representatives who voluntarily give of their time to distribute the envelopes and collect them. stay safe everyone. god bless and thank you. fr. john o’brien.
